items.question: Why can no being other than the Lord possess true agency?
premises: True agency consists only in knowledge, will, and effort.
No other factor constitutes agency beyond knowledge, will, and effort.
Therefore agency cannot belong to any other being at any time.
items.inference: Since agency is nothing but knowledge, will, and effort, no one other than the supreme agent can ever be a true doer.
items.plain_english: Agency is nothing other than knowledge, will, and effort; therefore no one else can ever possess true agency.

items.question: How is the Lord's autonomy related to the agency of individual selves?
premises: The wise know that the Lord's autonomy is agency.
Even the Lord's own agency is understood as autonomy.
This holds even when supreme lords or individual selves appear in difference.
items.inference: Agency is ultimately the Lord's autonomy, even when it appears distributed among distinct selves.
uncertainties: The phrase 'parameśānāṃ bhede bhede 'pi vātmanām' is compact; it may refer to apparent plurality among supreme lords and/or individual selves.
items.plain_english: The wise understand that the Lord's autonomy is agency; thus, even amid the apparent differences of supreme lords or individual selves, agency is that same autonomy.

items.question: Do actions bind beings by their own intrinsic nature?
premises: Actions do not arise for bondage by their own nature.
Good and bad results do not come from action by itself.
Therefore bondage and its results must be traced to another source.
items.inference: Since actions do not bind by their own nature, their good or bad fruits depend on a higher determining agency.
items.plain_english: Actions do not bind by their own nature; therefore this good or bad result does not arise merely from that action.

items.question: To whom does the sovereignty that determines karmic results belong?
premises: The sovereignty that determines results belongs to the supreme Lord alone.
This point has been conclusively established.
The author has elaborated it elsewhere.
items.inference: The power governing karmic outcomes is the exclusive sovereignty of the supreme Lord, as established in detail elsewhere.
items.plain_english: That sovereignty belongs to the supreme Lord alone; this has been determined and I have explained it at length elsewhere.

items.question: Why is the Lord's supreme power of action called Aghorā?
premises: The discussion returns to the main topic of the supreme power of action.
This supreme power belongs to the Lord.
It is proclaimed Aghorā because of its non-terrifying nature.
items.inference: The Lord's supreme power of action is designated Aghorā precisely because it is not terrifying.
items.plain_english: Enough of that; returning to the topic, this supreme power of action of the Lord is proclaimed Aghorā because of its non-terrifying nature.

rows.grounds: not limited to the self alone

items.question: What shows the benevolent character of this supreme power of action?
premises: This power is benevolent toward beings in their resort to Śiva.
Through it the path becomes direct and immediate.
The action it performs is not confined to a limited self.
items.inference: The supreme power of action is benevolent because it leads beings directly to Śiva through an action not restricted to the finite self.
uncertainties: The sense of 'sātmikā' here is read as 'self-centered/limited to the self'; context supports a contrast with universal grace.
items.plain_english: Therefore this power is benevolent: for beings who take refuge in Śiva it makes the path direct, and its action is not confined to a limited self.

rows.grounds: abiding in the state of Śiva

rows.morph: m.nom.sg (present passive participle √budh with causative sense)

items.question: How should one answer the objection that no beings here are established in Śiva-hood as agents?
premises: An objection claims that no beings here are established in Śiva-hood as agents.
The objection is conceded as true in a limited sense.
The instructed student should ascertain the matter in the proper way.
items.inference: Although no finite beings are independently established in Śiva-hood, the teaching must be understood in a way that preserves the Lord's agency.
items.plain_english: One may object that no beings here are established in Śiva-hood as agents; true, but the one being instructed should understand the matter properly.

items.question: What is the nature of the Lord and his power beyond limiting constructions?
premises: The Lord of gods is free from constructions of place, time, action, and form.
His power is likewise characterized.
That power is of universal form.
items.inference: Both the Lord and his power transcend limiting categories while the power manifests as the universe.
items.plain_english: The Lord of gods is free from constructions of place, time, action, and form; likewise his power is of universal form.

items.question: How can the universe be described if it abides in non-difference from Bhairava?
premises: The universe is also that same reality.
It is free from the stain-marks of time and other limiting factors.
It abides in non-difference from Bhairava.
items.inference: The universe, in its highest truth, is not limited by time and remains non-different from Bhairava.
uncertainties: The token '\hspace{3cm}' is editorial spacing, not a Sanskrit word; glossed minimally as spacer.
items.plain_english: That universe too is free from the stains of time and the rest, abiding in non-difference from Bhairava.

items.question: How does the universe remain autonomous and never outside Śiva-awareness?
premises: By the Lord's autonomy, the universe is autonomous.
It abides surging forth within itself.
Because it shines forth, it is never excluded from immersion in Śiva.
items.inference: The universe's manifestation is an autonomous expression within Śiva and never falls outside Śiva-awareness.
uncertainties: The compound 'astaśivāveśabahiṣkṛtam' is read as 'excluded from the loss of Śiva-immersion'; the negational layering is compact.
items.plain_english: By that autonomy it is autonomous, surging forth and abiding within itself; and because it shines, it is never excluded from immersion in Śiva.

items.question: Why is the supreme power described as both Dakṣiṇā and Aghorā?
premises: The supreme power is therefore both Dakṣiṇā and Aghorā in form.
Scripture will state that such powers grant the fruit of Śiva's abode.
This applies within the circle of beings.
items.inference: The supreme power's dual Dakṣiṇā-Aghorā nature is justified because it bestows the liberating fruit of Śiva's abode on beings.
items.plain_english: Therefore this supreme power has the form of both Dakṣiṇā and Aghorā, since it will be said to grant beings the fruit of Śiva's abode.

rows.grounds: present at the level of the limited being

items.question: How is Śiva's power of action described at the supreme and bound levels?
premises: Knowers of the doctrine declare the supreme Śiva-powers to be Aghorā.
Elsewhere the same power of action of Śiva operates in the bound soul.
The power of action thus functions at different levels.
items.inference: Śiva's power of action is supreme and Aghorā, yet it also operates within the condition of the bound soul.
items.plain_english: The knowers declare the supreme powers of Śiva to be Aghorā; and elsewhere Śiva's power of action operates within the bound soul.

items.question: How does the power of action function as both binding and liberating?
premises: The power of action binds when it abides in its own path.
When known, the same power brings about accomplishment.
This power is proclaimed as the expansion from A to Ha.
items.inference: The same phonemic expansion of the power of action binds in ignorance and grants accomplishment when known.
items.plain_english: Abiding in its own path it binds, but when known it brings accomplishment; it is proclaimed as the expansion from A to Ha.

items.question: How does the power of action unfold as the entire garland of letters?
premises: The same phonemic expansion proceeds from the abode of bindu.
It takes on the state of non-vowel manifestation.
This unfolding is the entire garland of letters.
items.inference: The whole alphabet is the unfolding of the power of action as it emanates from bindu into articulated phonemic form.
uncertainties: The phrase 'asvaratvam upāśritaḥ' is read in relation to consonantal manifestation from bindu; the exact technical nuance depends on the surrounding phonematic doctrine.
items.plain_english: That same expansion, proceeding from the abode of bindu and taking on non-vowel manifestation, is this unfolding of the power of action as the entire garland of letters.

items.question: What arises when the garland of letters is embraced by reflective I-awareness?
premises: The phonemic unfolding is embraced in the awareness 'I'.
This awareness has the nature of reflective self-consciousness.
From that arises the vivid flash of full supreme I-consciousness.
items.inference: When the power of action is gathered into reflective I-awareness, it manifests as the full supreme I-consciousness.
items.plain_english: Embraced in the reflective awareness 'I', it abides there; from that arises the vivid flash of the full, supreme I-consciousness.

rows.grounds: consuming the whole range of limited beings

items.question: How does the supreme I-consciousness relate to all beings and the universe?
premises: The supreme I-consciousness devours the mass of bound souls from Ananta to Brahmā.
It brings the moving and unmoving world into the cave of its own belly.
Thus all beings and worlds are contained within it.
items.inference: The supreme I-consciousness encompasses and reabsorbs the entire range of beings and the whole universe within itself.
items.plain_english: It devours the whole mass of bound souls from Ananta to Brahmā and draws the entire moving and unmoving world into the cave of its own belly.

items.question: Under what condition does the power of action manifest in this reabsorptive form?
premises: The supreme consciousness has swallowed the aggregate of individuals within its own reflective awareness.
It flashes forth dynamically.
As long as it flashes forth, it does so by the nature of the power of action.
items.inference: The dynamic flashing forth of reabsorptive consciousness is itself the operation of the power of action.
items.plain_english: Having swallowed the aggregate of individuals within the reflective awareness of its own consciousness, as long as it flashes forth, it does so by the nature of the power of action.

items.question: What kinds of differentiated states characterize this manifestation of the power of action?
premises: The manifestation includes countless varieties lacking full consciousness.
It also takes forms divided into gentle and fierce modes.
These modes include peace and endless activity among others.
items.inference: The power of action manifests as a vast spectrum of states, ranging from unconscious multiplicity to gentle and fierce divine modalities.
uncertainties: The compound analysis is dense; 'anantakāryaśānti' is read as 'endless activity and peace' as representative modalities.
items.plain_english: Its state is pervaded by countless unconscious varieties, and its nature is divided into gentle and fierce forms such as endless activity and peace.

items.question: Why do manifold forms arise from the splendor of Bhairava?
premises: Bhairava's splendor has a firm state revealed by the glory of its own reabsorption.
By appropriateness, manifold forms arise from it.
These varied forms do not contradict its stable nature.
items.inference: The manifold forms of manifestation arise appropriately from Bhairava's splendor, whose stability is grounded in its power of self-reabsorption.
items.plain_english: Even though its firm state is revealed by the glory of its own reabsorption, the splendor of Bhairava, by appropriateness, takes on various forms.

items.question: What characterizes the powers that arise from Bhairava's splendor?
premises: These powers are variegated by the recurrence of empty, full, and mixed states.
They are solely intent on reabsorbing their own portion called the universe.
Their reabsorption is into the nature of Śakti.
items.inference: The powers manifest in alternating modes yet are fundamentally oriented toward reabsorbing the universe into Śakti's nature.
items.plain_english: They are variegated by the recurrence of empty, full, and mixed states, and are solely intent on reabsorbing their own portion, called the universe, into the nature of Śakti.

items.question: How do the powers act to uproot long-entrenched worldly states?
premises: The powers are conditioned to uproot states long rooted in world and time.
From their own expansion they emit radiance.
Each power emits its own mass of rays.
items.inference: The powers uproot entrenched worldly conditions by radiating their own distinct expansions.
items.plain_english: Conditioned to uproot states long rooted in world and time, the powers, from their own expansion, send forth each its own mass of rays.

items.question: On what basis do the powers spread forth their fitting manifestations?
premises: The powers spread forth their own fitting manifestations.
They do so by relying on the true state of will.
Their operation is excluded from worldly left-hand practice.
items.inference: Grounded in efficacious will, the powers manifest what is fitting to them in a mode beyond ordinary worldly left-hand practice.
uncertainties: The compound 'lokotthavāmācārabahiṣkṛteḥ' is read as indicating exclusion from worldly left-hand practice; the doctrinal nuance may be more specific in context.
items.plain_english: Spreading forth, and relying on the true state of will, they manifest only what is fitting to them, in a way excluded from worldly left-hand practice.

items.question: How do the powers produce scriptures that reach fullness?
premises: The powers bring about scriptures.
These scriptures attain fullness.
Their model is the first-arisen teaching in the sphere of transcending the world.
items.inference: The powers fashion scriptures to fullness in accordance with the primordial teaching that transcends the world.
items.plain_english: They bring about scriptures that attain fullness, just like the first-arisen teaching in the sphere of transcending the world.

items.question: What is the nature of the practice and creation established here?
premises: The same transcendent practice appears here with the state of difference swallowed.
This is the full great creation of the supreme Lord.
That creation is established here.
items.inference: The practice established here is nondual, and it is identical with the supreme Lord's full great creation.
items.plain_english: That same practice here would be one in which the state of difference is swallowed; this is the full great creation of the supreme Lord, established here.
